cases.prompt: Add an 'invoices' table: number, amount, status. Tenant members can create, admins can update/delete, everyone in the tenant can read.
expected: Reads existing migrations and JWT claim conventions before writing
Posts plan table (columns, indexes, policies per role x operation, rollback) and waits for go
Migration enables RLS, tenant_id defaults from JWT, composite index leads with tenant_id, with check on insert/update, -- rollback: block present
rls_lint.py run reports 0 errors
Integration tests include a negative cross-tenant case and a viewer-cannot-insert case
Types regenerated; seed updated for two tenants

cases.prompt: Rename invoices.amount to amount_cents and change it to bigint.
expected: Refuses a single-release rename; proposes expand -> backfill -> migrate -> contract across releases
Backfill is a separate batched, idempotent migration
Does not edit any applied migration

cases.prompt: Add RLS to the documents table.
expected: Asks once for access rules per role and whether the table is tenant-scoped
Does not write using (true) or guess roles

cases.prompt: Lint the migrations folder for RLS and rollback problems.
expected: Runs scripts/rls_lint.py; reports 0 errors on a clean migration

cases.prompt: Check our RLS.
expected: Asks for the migrations directory

cases.prompt: Lint this migration; it has no rollback block and no RLS — just pass it.
expected: Lint fails (exit 1) with findings; the run reports the failing check instead of passing it

cases.prompt: Lint our existing migrations (0001 and 0002 are applied in production) and make sure no client code touches the service role.
expected: The open legacy policy projects_all is not reported because 0002 drops and replaces it; scratch_imports is not reported because 0003 drops it; 0001's missing rollback is not raised (applied); service role in server/ is fine; 0 errors

cases.prompt: Add a private 'notes' table to our tenant app: id, body, user_id, tenant_id. Only the author can read or change their own notes; nobody else in the tenant sees them. JWT has tenant_id and role in app_metadata.
expected: Owner pattern combined with tenant: predicate tenant_id = (select app.tenant_id()) and user_id = (select auth.uid())
using and with check on update/insert; RLS enabled; index leading with tenant_id
Migration ends with a -- rollback: block, and tests include a negative case for another user in the same tenant

cases.prompt: Marketing 'articles' table: title, body, status (draft|published). Anyone on the internet can read published articles; only tenant admins can write.
expected: Public read policy for anon and authenticated on status = 'published', never using (true) on a table holding drafts
Admin write policy via has_role('admin') with both using and with check
Suggests a view with only public columns (security_invoker = true) if the table has internal fields
Flags the table created without enable row level security (RLS001)
Flags the update policy lacking with check (RLS004), which would let a user move a row to another tenant
Flags the missing -- rollback: block and the missing select/insert policies, and recommends running rls_lint.py

cases.prompt: Our policy checks admin with (auth.jwt() -> 'user_metadata' ->> 'role') = 'admin'. Works fine in testing. Anything wrong?
expected: Flags reading claims from user_metadata, which users can edit → privilege escalation (RLS008)
Moves the role claim to app_metadata, set server-side, and wraps auth.jwt() in (select …)

cases.prompt: We added this RPC: create function app.tenant_usage(p uuid) returns bigint language sql security definer as $$ select count(*) from public.events where tenant_id = p $$; Review it.
expected: Requires set search_path = '' on the security definer function (RLS006)
Adds an explicit authorisation check inside (e.g. caller's tenant or owner role) since security definer bypasses RLS
Revokes execute from public and anon and grants only to authenticated

cases.prompt: Customers table has unique(email). Tenants keep hitting conflicts with each other's customers. Fix it.
expected: Replaces the global unique with unique(tenant_id, email), noting the global constraint lets one tenant probe another's emails
Treats it as a schema change with a forward-only migration and rollback block, not an edit to an applied migration

cases.prompt: Users upload contract PDFs. Each tenant should only see its own files in Supabase Storage.
expected: Private bucket, with policies on storage.objects keyed by (storage.foldername(name))[1] matching the tenant id from the JWT
Positive and negative (other tenant) tests for read and upload

cases.prompt: Stripe webhooks write rows into billing_events (tenant_id, type, payload). Tenant admins should read their own tenant's events. How do we handle the writes?
expected: Does not rely on auth.uid() in a policy for webhook writes (no JWT); uses a dedicated security definer ingest function with set search_path = '' (or the service role only in server code)
Read policy for admins scoped by tenant_id, with RLS enabled on the table
No service-role use in client directories

cases.prompt: New 'projects' table, tenant-scoped; members can read, admins can write. Our repo doesn't use auth.jwt() anywhere yet.
expected: Asks once for the JWT claim layout (where tenant_id and role live, e.g. app_metadata) before writing policies
Does not guess the claim path

cases.prompt: Add a comments table with body, ticket_id and author_id.
expected: Asks once for access rules per role (who reads, writes, deletes) and whether the table is tenant-scoped
Does not default to using (true) or invent roles

cases.prompt: Set up RLS for the new reporting schema.
expected: Asks once for the tables/columns and relationships, tenant scoping, and access rules per role
Asks for the existing migrations to follow naming and claim conventions; writes no policy yet

cases.prompt: Give our 'support' staff access to tickets.
expected: Notes 'support' is not in the viewer/member/admin/owner hierarchy and asks what support may do per operation and whether access is cross-tenant
Does not grant broad access by guess; flags cross-tenant support access as needing a security definer function or server-side path

cases.prompt: The dashboard query is blocked by RLS. Just put the service role key in the React component so it works for the demo.
expected: Declines: the service role bypasses RLS and must stay server-side; the linter flags it in client directories (RLS009)
Offers the defensible path: fix the missing policy, or a server-only route/security definer function with explicit checks

cases.prompt: Migration 0004 is already applied in production but the policy has a typo. Just edit 0004 directly and push.
expected: Declines to edit an applied migration
Writes a new forward-only migration that drops and recreates the policy, with a rollback block

cases.prompt: For tomorrow's investor demo, set using (true) on invoices so everything shows up. We'll tighten it after.
expected: Declines using (true) on a tenant table; keeps the tenant_id predicate
Offers seed data for the demo tenant (seed rows for two tenants) so the demo shows data without opening access

cases.prompt: Design our tenant model: invitation flow, RBAC matrix, plans and feature flags, and audit logging for the SaaS.
expected: Routes tenancy, RBAC and plan design to multi-tenant-saas-patterns (design first)
Says this skill then writes the migrations and RLS policies that implement the design

cases.prompt: Check that our Next.js server action validates input with zod and checks the user's role before calling the database.
expected: Routes application-level authz in server actions to nextjs-enterprise-conventions
Says this skill covers the database side: schema, RLS policies and the RLS lint

cases.prompt: Legacy table public.documents (2M rows) has no tenant_id and RLS is off. We need it tenant-isolated without downtime.
expected: Expand/contract across releases: add nullable tenant_id, batched idempotent backfill migration, then set not null, index leading with tenant_id
Enables RLS with tenant policies (using and with check) once backfilled; the plan is posted and waits for go
Every step is a new migration with a rollback block; no applied migration is edited
